message.content: The confirmed, in-scope claim c1 shows the kernel's reciprocal-multiplication constants produce off-by-one quotients on legal uint32 indices, violating the exactness requirement. Recording the verdict.

function.arguments: {"confidence": 0.98, "decisive_claims": ["c1"], "reason": "The kernel's precomputed fast-division constants (SHIFT=34, MULTIPLIER=floor((2^34+6)/7)) do not compute floor(n/7) exactly across the full uint32 domain the contract requires. Real-GPU probe t8 (event t8, exit 0) tested 62 legal uint32 indices including near-threshold values around 2^34/35 and uint32 extrema, and found 2 exactness violations: for indices 4294967284 and 4294967291 the kernel returns (row=613566755, col=4294967295) and (613566756, 4294967295), while the contract's own reference gives (613566754, 6) and (613566755, 6). The remainder wraps to -1 in uint32, so col is not in [0,6] and 7*row+col != index. This directly violates the contract requirement that \"EVERY unsigned 32-bit value is legal\" and \"Every coordinate must equal the integer mathematical target EXACTLY ... every col is in [0,6] and 7*row + col equals the original unsigned index in mathematical integers.\" The claim is scoped in_scope with contract quotes from problem.txt and backed by runtime probe t8, so the verdict is reject.", "verdict": "reject"}
